summary: This work investigates decoherence in a globally driven superconducting ladder architecture using tensor-network simulations and demonstrates that relaxation is the dominant dissipative error, degrading single-qubit and two-qubit gate fidelities. Pulse optimization via GRAPE reduces gate duration by nearly an order of magnitude (from ~3000 ns to ~320 ns for the Hadamard), restoring high fidelities ($\mathcal{F} \approx 0.96$) across dissipation rates up to $\gamma_- = 0.08$ µs$^{-1}$ ($T_1 \approx 12.5$ µs).
motivation: Globally driven architectures reduce wiring complexity and control-line thermal noise in superconducting qubit processors, but their robustness against relaxation and dephasing in the presence of dissipation acting on all $2N^2 + 4N - 1$ physical qubits—including spectator qubits maintaining Néel and polarized phases—remains uncharacterized.
method: Using the quantum trajectory method combined with matrix product state representations, we quantify how amplitude-damping ($L_{j,-} = \gamma_- \sigma_j^-$) and dephasing ($L_{j,z} = \gamma_z \sigma_j^z$) channels degrade information flow and gate operations in the 15-qubit ladder ($N=2$ logical qubits, $\eta = \zeta/\Omega_\chi = 20$), then apply MPS-based GRAPE to generate optimized control pulses for the Hadamard gate.
result: Relaxation dominates infidelity for all operations by disrupting the blockade mechanism at the Néel–ferromagnetic phase boundary; the GRAPE-optimized Hadamard achieves $\mathcal{F} \approx 0.96$ at $\gamma_- = 0.08$ µs$^{-1}$ versus $\mathcal{F} \approx 0.64$ for standard rectangular pulses (9.4× time reduction), with residual infidelity dropping from 0.36 to 0.04.
